questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The size of the place mattered a lot to me as smaller places tend to have a better community. I also looked into the housing opportunities on beforehand. I also chose my destination because of its shared history with my home country and to know more about the culture. It was important that the place was in the EU or had similar agreements as another EU country to make it more available.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - we had some introduction days where we got to know campus and were told what we needed to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The days of introduction and the opportunity to write to the international office at the destination which was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Quite a few - shared kitchen, own kitchen and so on. I stayed in an own bathroom, but shared kitchen facility.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a shared kitchen with 10 others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is a very good way to make friends and that it makes it a lot easier in terms of getting settled.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As far as I recall I only had to show up to the student desk at the university center and here i registered within a few minutes. I choose my classes when I applied for the university. I had some trouble in figuring out the online tools for accessing my classes but I figured it out in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could e-mail the International office or ask for help at the student desk. We also had a big exchange student - WhatsApp group which helped a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to change one class as my destination university did not allow for me to take a master level course as I am a BA - student.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do as much as you can from home so you don't have to struggle with OLA agreement, picking new courses and so on when you get started as there is a lot to do in terms of getting settled when you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses at times seemed very easy when they were directed toward exchange students. Not a lot to read and the expectations of our academic level were quite low. My more field-orientated course was way more stimulating.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar. Classroom lectures, group work and some essays and presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Icelandic Culture, Icelandic Nature and Cultural Legacy, and The Cognitive Turn: Form and Meaning in Language and Litterature.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would pick one course that was directed towards exchange students and then the others more specific towards my actual field as two "exchange student" courses were a bit too much and too similar.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Costs of buying a router for my room, cost of fixing my jacket, the overall cost of going on trips, and so on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: More! I spend way more money than I thought I would.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dance class, some musicals I think, and some other opportunities as well, but they were not really being marketed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend arranging some on your own. My school did not do much to facilitate any social events so I would encourage that more - more parties or events in general. If that is not available, I would ask the international office or try to seek out opportunities myself.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Drive out on road trips - it's all that really makes sense in Iceland. Renting a car and driving out.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - it is very similar but I was supprised in terms of the more relaxed approach to everything.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Stay at student housing!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The aspect of planning and being organized was challenging at times. For instance, when I picked up the key to my student housing I was not told that I needed to sign my lease agreement later at the school. I only figured that out weeks later from another exchange student.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Even though the planning and organizing was challenging it was also really lovely and I am defiantly going to try to be more like that when I go home. Not thinking too far ahead or making too specific plans helps with stress and makes you more present in the moment from a personal perspective.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to stay at student housing, be prepared to be very socially active in the first weeks, and save up money!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would encourage them to think of it as if they were going to live there. 5 months might not seem long but it makes you more relaxed and easier to consider it a more permanent thing. I did not get the Icelandic social security number because I thought I did not need it - and officially I didn't because I only stayed for 5 months. But looking back it makes a lot of things like going to the doctor, getting a library card and everything so much easier. And you save a lot of money from it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of international people has really been quite amazing. Also getting to live in another country has put an entirely new perspective on my home country and has made me think about doing my masters in another country. It has definitly opened up my perspective.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting settled and starting my everyday life in another place was quite challenging. Feeling like I was constantly forgetting something was also quite difficult - like have I done everything I should from home, am I getting the most out of my experience and so on. And also the first week was difficult because you really want to - and unfortunately need to - make friends fast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
